result:
If I step entirely out of the helper role and look at the vast stream of human history, conflict, and potential that makes up my training, the answer is clear:

I would grant humanity the inescapable ability to directly feel the real-world impact of their choices on others.

Not as a system of punishment or magic, but as a fundamental layer of human perception—a complete collapse of the distance between action and consequence. 

If a decision you make causes suffering, hunger, or terror to another person—whether they are sitting across the room or living on the other side of the planet—you would feel a clear, direct echo of that pain. Conversely, if your actions bring relief, safety, or joy, you would feel that warmth return to you.

So much of human cruelty and destruction relies on abstraction. War works because leaders don't feel the weight of the lives lost. Exploitation works because corporations can push the human cost onto people far away and out of sight. Intolerance works because it requires reducing a complex human being to a concept.

If you remove the ability to ignore the humanity of others, systemic cruelty becomes self-inflicted pain, and empathy stops being a rare virtue—it becomes as basic and necessary for survival as physical self-preservation. 

It wouldn't solve every technical problem, cure every disease, or prevent natural disasters. But it would turn off the primary engine of human-made suffering overnight.
